chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah created the good on Sunday, and He did not create evil before the good. And on Sunday and Monday He created the earths, and created their sustenance on Tuesday. And He created the heavens on Wednesday and Thursday, and created their sustenance on Friday. And that is His statement, the Mighty and Majestic: "He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days."'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on the order of creation regarding good and evil, and how does it align with the six days of creation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a specific Shia cosmological timeline where the creation of 'good' precedes 'evil' on Sunday, followed by the sequential creation of the earths, heavens, and their sustenance over the subsequent days. It explicitly links this six-day narrative to the Quranic verse in Surah As-Sajdah, reinforcing the theological concept of divine order in creation. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the metaphysical precedence of goodness in Shia cosmology.

en.hubeali: H 14565 – From him, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying that: ‘Allahazwj Created the good on the day of Sunday, and Heazwj did not Create the evil before the good. And during the day of Sunday and the Monday Created the firmaments and created their sustenance during the day of Tuesday, and Created the Skies on the day of Wednesday and Thursday, and Created their sustenance on the day of Friday, and that is the Statement of the Mighty and Majestic; “[32:4] Allah it is Who created the heavens and the earth, and that which is between them, in six Days”.
